title: Efficient Approximation Algorithms for Spanning Centrality

problem.claim: Computing the spanning centrality of all edges in large graphs is highly challenging.

gap.claim: Existing techniques rely on expensive matrix operations or numerous long random walks and fail to handle large graphs effectively.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes TGT and TGT+, two algorithms for computing the spanning centrality of all edges.
TGT uses deterministic graph traversals with carefully designed truncated lengths.
TGT+ combines TGT with random walks and additional heuristic optimizations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: TGT and TGT+ provide rigorous theoretical approximation guarantees.
TGT+ is reported to improve empirical efficiency and asymptotic performance while retaining result quality.
On a variety of real datasets, TGT+ is reported to outperform recent competitors, often with over one order of magnitude speedup without degrading accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spanning centrality measures an edge's importance for graph connectivity.
Spanning centrality has practical applications, but computing it for all edges on large graphs is difficult.
Existing approaches are limited by expensive matrix operations or many long random walks.
The paper introduces TGT and TGT+, using deterministic truncated traversals and an enhanced combination with random walks and heuristics.
TGT+ is experimentally compared with recent competitors on real datasets and is reported to achieve substantial speedups without accuracy degradation.

The graph-size conditions and scalability limits are not stated.
